title: Fibber McGee and Molly
paragraphs: A landmark radio comedy following Fibber and Molly McGee in the fictional town of Wistful Vista, surrounded by recurring neighbors, running gags, and Fibber's endless schemes.
Jim and Marian Jordan’s long-running NBC comedy centered on 79 Wistful Vista.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Weekly half-hour era (April 16, 1935 to June 30, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], 15-minute weekday strip era (October 5, 1953 to March 23, 1956) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Monitor sketch era (June 1, 1957 to September 6, 1959) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|jim-jordan|Jim Jordan]] (performer), [[person|marian-jordan|Marian Jordan]] (performer), Phil Leslie (writer), [[person|bill-thompson|Bill Thompson]] (performer), Arthur Q. Bryan (performer), Max Hutto (director and performer), and Harlow Wilcox (performer and announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.a1cc4e5534fec5a3|WMAQ]].
The stories often return to Neighbors and community, Household life, Civic life and local authority, Money and consumer life, Holiday episodes, and Fibber’s schemes and tall tales.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Radio domestic comedy during the Depression, Wartime American home-front comedy, and Network radio transition to short-form Monitor features.
